blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Philippine banks remain healthy and well-capitalized despite mounting economic challenges, supported by strong regulatory oversight from the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP), Moody’s Ratings said. In a report dated Oct. 29, the global debt watcher assigned the Philippines a banking sector risk score of “a,” matching those of Colombia, India, Indonesia and Malaysia. READ: BSP wants easier rules on banks’ liquidity facility Moody’s said the country’s banking system remained well-capitalized, profitable and competently managed, reducing the risk of widespread financial sector distress that could force the fiscally constrained government to step in.
